title: Colour token layer for WCAG contrast certification
description:
Objective: give the control room resolvable colour values, so the spec's "Contrast >= WCAG AA" clause becomes measurable instead of unmeasurable.

WHY THIS EXISTS (project rail 4, Clause 2 gap measurement). Spec section 11.1 line 686 requires "Contrast >= WCAG AA". A contrast ratio needs two RESOLVED colours. At planning time the architect probed for any colour value on disk and found NONE:
- TruthSemanticTone is a PROSE union, not colour: packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts carries "neutral slate", "amber", "green", "blue", "high-contrast magenta" as semanticTone strings. Those name a colour; they are not one.
- Zero hex, rgb(), hsl() or oklch() literals exist in apps/control-room/src or in any packages/*/src.
- The repo contains exactly ONE stylesheet, apps/control-room/src/board/board-layout.css (77 lines), and it uses only the CSS system keywords canvas and highlight. className count across the app is 0 and there is no CSS-in-JS dependency.

Two tasks have already had to record contrast as explicitly NOT mechanically checkable because of this:
- task-4b274fad (Motion and colour-independence regression guards) excludes it in its DoD with this reason.
- task-667b1085 (Control-room journey gate) inherited real-browser contrast certification from task-ab8c9489 via governor comment comment-5dd36b5b, and cannot discharge it while no colour resolves.

This task closes that hole once, for both.

IMPORTANT — this is NOT a visual redesign, and epic scope forbids one. The app renders essentially unstyled today. The deliverable is a token layer that makes the EXISTING semantic tones resolve to concrete, AA-compliant values against a named background, in light and dark. Do not restyle surfaces, do not introduce a component library, and do not change any layout.

Owned paths: the token stylesheet and its test, plus the semanticTone-to-token mapping. Do NOT edit describeTruthClass's five descriptors: their glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle are pinned by CR-A11Y-001, which asserts the classes stay distinguishable with colour EXCLUDED.

Hard dependencies: none blocking.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test
definitionOfDone: Every TruthSemanticTone prose value maps to a concrete foreground colour token and a named background token, in both light and dark. The mapping is exhaustive over the union and a test asserts exhaustiveness — adding a sixth tone without a token must fail the build or the test, never default silently.

A test computes the actual WCAG contrast ratio for every foreground/background token pair and asserts it meets AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and non-text indicators). It must assert the number of pairs checked is greater than zero and equals the number of declared tones, so a sweep over an empty or partial token set cannot pass.

The contrast computation is asserted against the production token values, not against a table restated inside the test. A test that recomputes its own expected colours proves only that the test is self-consistent.
A tone with no token, or a token that fails AA, produces a stable reason code naming the offending tone and ratio — the test asserts that specific code, not merely that something failed.

describeTruthClass's five descriptors are unchanged: glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle are untouched, and the committed CR-A11Y-001 monochrome check still passes, proving the classes remain distinguishable with colour excluded. Colour is added as a fourth channel, never as a replacement for the other three.

No layout, spacing or component structure changes. The only stylesheet edits are token declarations, every stylesheet carrying tokens also carries a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block per the existing board-layout.css:68 pattern, and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test passes.
taskRails: Pinned UI spec: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-v1-control-room-spec.md SHA-256 C55AF8A9FC7386E6492FD57E34A4B8321ABAAE4E4E08FF38703544B58B0BEF1F. Contrast is section 11.1 line 686; the truth-class tones are section 3.1; section 13.1 limits theming to light/dark plus monochrome survival and forbids visual tokens beyond section 3's semantics.

Colour is never the only carrier. Spec section 3.1 requires triple encoding — glyph, short label, colour — surviving monochrome, colour-vision deficiency and screen readers. This task adds the third channel; it must not weaken the first two. CR-A11Y-001 asserts the five classes stay distinguishable by glyph + label + border with colour EXCLUDED, and that test must still pass unchanged.

jsdom evaluates no CSS and document.styleSheets.length is 0 because Vitest stubs the CSS import (measured). Contrast must therefore be computed from the TOKEN VALUES as data — exported constants the stylesheet is generated from or pinned against — not by reading computed style from a rendered element. If the tokens live only as CSS text, the test must parse the real file and assert it parsed a non-zero number of declarations.

This is not a redesign. The app is deliberately near-unstyled and epic scope excludes visual redesign outside the pinned spec. Adding component styling, a design system, or a dependency is out of scope and will be rejected.
Split before 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.

implementationPlan.description:
UNDERSTAND THE REAL GAP before writing. The colour layer EXISTS; what is missing is that nothing DERIVES from it. The production chain is complete and three links long:

  TruthSemanticTone (prose union, packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts:12-17)
    -> surfaces.css:20-40   button[data-testid^="cr.chip."][data-tone="<prose>"] { background: var(--cr-truth-*) }
    -> tokens.css:21-25     --cr-truth-observed #5e6d74, -agent #9a621b, -verified #176f5b, -human #3c65d4, -unknown #b33b8f
  Foreground: surfaces.css:5  color: #ffffff  on the chip base rule (a real pair, not fictional).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN — styles/design-system.test.ts:64-71 computes contrast over HARDCODED HEX LITERALS written inside the test. It never reads a value out of tokens.css. That is precisely what DoD 3 forbids: "a table restated inside the test proves only that the test is self-consistent." The neighbouring pin at :50-62 does assert tokens.css CONTAINS those literals, so the pair is coupled today — but it pins only 13 of ~35 light tokens and 2 of 13 dark overrides, and it is a pin, not a derivation.

FOUR CONCRETE HOLES this task closes:
  a. No exhaustiveness over TruthSemanticTone. design-system.test.ts:73-80 loops a RESTATED list of five tone strings. Add a sixth tone to the union and nothing fails — DoD 1 requires the build or a test to break.
  b. Contrast never resolves a production token value (DoD 3).
  c. No assertion that the number of pairs checked is non-zero and equals the tone count (DoD 2).
  d. No stable reason code naming the offending tone and ratio (DoD 4).

DARK MODE, MEASURED: tokens.css:38 is the ONLY prefers-color-scheme block in the app and it contains ZERO --cr-truth-* overrides, so the five tones are byte-identical in light and dark while the canvas flips to #111820 / surface #18212b. Chips are filled with the tone and use white text in both modes, so the pair is unchanged — defensible, but currently true by accident. DoD 1 requires it asserted deliberately for both modes.

DoD 1 — create the semanticTone-to-token mapping as TYPED DATA, the artifact the whole certification derives from.

New file apps/control-room/src/styles/truth-tone-tokens.ts exporting:

  export interface TruthToneTokenPair { readonly background: string; readonly foreground: string; }
  export const TRUTH_TONE_TOKENS: Record<TruthSemanticTone, TruthToneTokenPair>

Import TruthSemanticTone as a TYPE-ONLY import from @moe/control-room-model. Do NOT edit that package — DoD 5 forbids touching describeTruthClass, and a type-only import keeps the blast radius inside this app.

Values are CSS CUSTOM PROPERTY NAMES, never hex: e.g. "neutral slate" -> { background: "--cr-truth-observed", foreground: "--cr-white" }. Hex belongs in tokens.css and nowhere else; duplicating it here would recreate the restated-table defect this task exists to fix.

WHY Record<TruthSemanticTone, ...> AND NOT A PLAIN OBJECT: this is the DoD 1 "must fail the BUILD" arm. Adding a sixth member to the union makes tsc fail on the missing key, so a tone can never default silently. Verify that claim in step 7 by actually adding a temporary sixth member and confirming `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` fails.

Use --cr-white (tokens.css:19, #ffffff) as the named foreground token. Note in a comment that surfaces.css:5 currently writes the literal #ffffff rather than var(--cr-white); step 4 asserts the two resolve equal, which is how the mapping stays honest WITHOUT editing surfaces.css. Do not change that literal — DoD 6 permits token-declaration edits only.

DoD 2, 3, 4 — create apps/control-room/src/styles/truth-tone-contrast.test.ts, the certification that resolves PRODUCTION values. Per the task rail, jsdom evaluates no CSS and document.styleSheets.length is 0, so parse the real files as text; the rail explicitly permits this provided the parse is proven non-empty.

Parse, asserting each parse is live BEFORE using it:
  1. tokens.css -> Map<customProperty, hex>. Assert size > 0 and that the five --cr-truth-* keys plus --cr-white resolved. Parse the :root block and the prefers-color-scheme: dark block SEPARATELY so a dark override is applied only where it exists.
  2. surfaces.css -> Map<prose tone, custom property> by matching [data-tone="X"] rules and their `background: var(--Y)`. Assert size > 0.
  3. surfaces.css chip base rule -> its `color:` value. Assert it equals the resolved --cr-white value; this is what licenses treating white as the production foreground.

Then assert the parsed CSS mapping EQUALS TRUTH_TONE_TOKENS from step 3, both directions. This is the anti-drift link: the typed map cannot silently diverge from the stylesheet, and the stylesheet cannot silently diverge from the map.

Contrast: reuse the sRGB relative-luminance formula already proven in design-system.test.ts:17-33 (channel/luminance/contrast). Compute every foreground/background pair from the RESOLVED hex, for light AND dark. Assert >= 4.5 (normal text). If any pair is only intended to clear the 3:1 large-text/non-text bar, assert 3.0 for that pair explicitly and comment why — never silently lower the global threshold.

DoD 2 count assertions, both required: pairs checked > 0, AND pairs checked === the number of members in TRUTH_TONE_TOKENS === the number of [data-tone] rules parsed from surfaces.css. A sweep over a partial or empty token set must fail.

DoD 4 reason codes — return violations as frozen { code, tone, ratio } and assert the SPECIFIC code, never merely that something failed:
  CR-CONTRAST-001  tone declared in the union with no resolvable token
  CR-CONTRAST-002  resolved pair below its AA threshold (carry the measured ratio)
  CR-CONTRAST-003  typed map and parsed stylesheet disagree
Assert the happy path as a whole-object equality on an empty violations array with the expected checked count, so an extra violation cannot slip past a `.length` check.

DoD 5 — prove colour was added as a FOURTH channel, never a replacement, and that this task touched none of the other three.

The DoD names "CR-A11Y-001". That reason code DOES NOT EXIST in the repo (step 1 measurement). The real committed predicate is auditTruthClassMonochrome in src/a11y/surface-audit.ts, whose codes are TRUTH_CLASS_COUNT_MISMATCH and TRUTH_CLASS_MONOCHROME_COLLISION. It deliberately excludes semanticTone and compares only glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle. Name the real symbol in the test and in your completion evidence; state the DoD's code name is stale so QA does not read it as a missing deliverable.

Assert, in the new contrast test:
  - auditTruthClassMonochrome() returns { checked: 5, violations: [] }, consuming the production predicate. Do NOT reimplement it (it is already asserted at a11y/colour-independence.test.tsx:223 — consistent, not duplicated).
  - describeTruthClass's five descriptors are unchanged: glyph, shortLabel and borderStyle byte-identical to HEAD. Prove it in the diff, not only by assertion — `git diff HEAD -- packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts` must be EMPTY at completion.

The monochrome predicate passing while the colour layer is certified is the whole point: the classes stay distinguishable with colour excluded AND now also carry AA-compliant colour.

DoD 6 — no layout change, and resolve the reduced-motion clause, which is INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY as written.

DoD 6 requires (i) "the only stylesheet edits are token declarations" and (ii) "every stylesheet carrying tokens also carries a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block". tokens.css carries tokens and has NO such block; adding one would itself be a stylesheet edit that is not a token declaration, breaking (i) to satisfy (ii).

RESOLVE IT THE WAY THE GOVERNOR ALREADY RULED, do not add the block. governor-42b952c9 ratified at 18:37Z on task-4b274fadc (governors channel msg-f91f6d76788e4ceb82fe19d7b35e3bf8) that this app gates motion with ONE global universal reset in styles/responsive.css, imported from styles/control-room.css, and that per-stylesheet blocks are NOT required: "Do not require a same-stylesheet @media block." tokens.css additionally contains ZERO motion declarations — --cr-ease is a timing-function VALUE that no rule in tokens.css applies.

So assert COVERAGE instead of a redundant block: tokens.css is imported by control-room.css, and control-room.css imports responsive.css whose universal reset neutralises animation and transition with !important. The committed guard a11y/motion-inventory.test.ts already asserts exactly this; reference it rather than duplicating it.

Record this reading and the ratification in a comment in the new test file so QA inherits it.

No-layout-change proof: the final diff must contain only the two NEW files from steps 3 and 4. If any .css appears in `git diff --stat` over owned paths, something went wrong. This task is expected to change ZERO existing stylesheets.

MUTATION VERIFICATION — a certification that cannot go red certifies nothing. Run all four drills, one at a time, reverting fully after each and confirming green again before the next. Record the exact failing assertion for each.

  1. BUILD EXHAUSTIVENESS (DoD 1): add a temporary sixth member to TruthSemanticTone in packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` MUST fail on the missing Record key. This is the only drill that touches an unowned package — revert it immediately and verify with `git diff HEAD -- packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts` returning EMPTY.
  2. CONTRAST (CR-CONTRAST-002): change --cr-truth-verified in tokens.css from #176f5b to a light value such as #d8f5ec. The new test MUST go red naming the tone and the measured ratio. NOTE: design-system.test.ts:50-62 will also go red because it pins that literal — expected, and it confirms the two tests are complementary rather than duplicates.
  3. DRIFT (CR-CONTRAST-003): change the tone key in one surfaces.css [data-tone] rule so the stylesheet and the typed map disagree. MUST go red.
  4. PARSE LIVENESS: point the tokens.css reader at a nonexistent path. The parse-is-non-empty assertion MUST fail rather than the suite passing over zero declarations.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD, and it has bitten this board repeatedly today: another agent's completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it is on disk. After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof if a foreign commit captured the bytes. Drills 1 and 2 touch files this task does not own — never leave either mutated.

Verification and adversarial review. Run the named gate and use its FRESH output as complete_task evidence:

  pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test

Baseline for comparison: 44 files / 622 tests passing, measured 18:41Z before this task began. Your run must show 45 files and a higher test count; a flat file count means the new test never ran.

FOCUSED RUNS — DO NOT PASS --config. apps/control-room has NO vitest.config.* file, so `--config package.json` silently discards the jsdom environment and produces a convincing FALSE RED of "ReferenceError: document is not defined". Correct form: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run src/styles/truth-tone-contrast.test.ts`. Tell-tale of the broken form is `environment 0ms` in the summary.

Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` — the Record exhaustiveness arm is a compile-time property and the test run alone does not prove it.

Path-attributed baseline per project rail: record repo-wide failures at merge-base and at HEAD; the (HEAD minus merge-base) failing set intersected with owned paths must be EMPTY. Foreign red outside @moe/control-room is disclosed verbatim, never hidden, never fabricated green. Foreign red INSIDE @moe/control-room is a block, not a disclosure.

Adversarial review before complete_task:
- Would any assertion pass over zero cases? Re-check every parse-liveness and count precondition actually fires.
- Is any expected colour written in the test rather than resolved from tokens.css? That is the exact defect this task exists to fix — grep the new test for hex literals and justify every survivor.
- Did I edit a stylesheet? I must not have. Owned-path `git diff --stat` should show exactly two NEW files.
- Is packages/control-room-model/src/index.ts byte-identical to HEAD after drill 1?
- Line caps: target 250, split before 400, measured with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object -Line undercounts by skipping blank lines).
- Stage and commit by EXPLICIT pathspec over the two new files only. Never git add -A.
